clue.text: Charles followed Mary

definitions.meaning: Charles ... was the English essayist who wrote as Elia
in the nursery rhyme, the little woolly animal Mary had followed her to school

explanation.surface: A man named Charles trailed after a woman called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings point at the same surname: the essayist Charles, and the young sheep of 'Mary had a little ...', which followed her everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the essayist's surname; the other is the young sheep that, in the nursery rhyme, trailed its owner Mary to school.

clue.text: Most valuable greeting for new employee

definitions.text: Most valuable greeting for new employee

parts.words: Most valuable greeting for new employee
parts.note: read literally, a greeting of the most precious metal; in business, a lump-sum payment offered to lure a recruit

explanation.definitionFit: A cash sum paid to a recruit on joining a firm is jokingly called the precious-metal version of a welcome.

clue.text: One deity entered Pennsylvania building

indicators.note: one piece entering the state's abbreviation means it is placed inside it

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
one is A, the indefinite article
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A single god has moved into a structure in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower, typically a temple in East Asia, is a kind of building.

clue.text: Imagine eccentric one of the pack

parts.note: to imagine something is to picture it
an eccentric person is a card, informally

explanation.surface: Picture an oddball member of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' as a noun for a comic or odd person is informal British usage; 'pack' here means a deck of playing cards, not a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A king, queen or jack is a member of a deck of playing cards bearing a figure.

clue.text: Nonsense, one starts with crude laugh

parts.note: guff is informal for nonsense or empty talk
one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word with starts something, so only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone spouting rubbish follows it up with a vulgar laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letter of 'with', W, to finish the word after GUFF and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, coarse, hearty burst of laughter is exactly a rough guffaw-type laugh, the kind the clue calls crude.

clue.text: Ruled fad out that's awesome

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A craze has been dismissed as impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RULED FAD. 'Awesome' is used in its old sense of inspiring awe or dread, not the modern 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words originally meant inspiring fear or dread, before softening into everyday senses.

clue.text: Left harbour

definitions.meaning: the left side of a ship is the ... side
a harbour town or haven for ships is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, facing forward, the left side is port; and a harbour where ships dock is a port.

clue.text: One short walk round in golf competition

indicators.note: the short walk goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: PROM is short for promenade, a seaside walk
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single brief stroll around a golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: PROM is promenade cut short, so 'short' belongs with 'walk'; 'round' puts PROM around A. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament pairing professionals with amateur players is a common golf event format.

clue.text: Got up most of trendy substance used in varnish

indicators.note: only most of the word for got up is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: got up means rose
something trendy is in

explanation.surface: Someone got up to put a fashionable ingredient into wood finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' reads as a verb in the surface story but is a past-tense synonym, and 'most of' cuts its final letter; 'trendy' supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: This resin, left after distilling turpentine from pine, goes into varnishes and is rubbed on violin bows.

clue.text: High-class oil mixed to make dressing

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or high-class, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of oil are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Quality oil is whisked to produce a salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 becomes AI by reading the 1 as I; 'mixed' turns OIL into OLI. 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This garlic mayonnaise from Provence is served as a sauce or dressing with fish and vegetables.

clue.text: Home of a hot drink?

parts.note: read literally, a dwelling where a hot beverage lives; really, a place where that beverage is served

explanation.definitionFit: A café selling espresso and similar brews is jokingly the residence of that drink.

clue.text: I had taken chance going round basin

indicators.note: going round means the gamble word encloses the other piece

parts.note: to have taken a chance is to bet
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: I gambled on a trip around a washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basin' suggests a kitchen sink, but the bathroom fixture is meant; 'going round' tells the gamble to wrap around the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A low bathroom fixture for washing oneself is a kind of basin.

clue.text: Rebelling as well before arriving, likely to succeed

parts.note: people rebelling are up, as in risen up or up in arms
as well means and, adding something
arriving means coming

explanation.surface: A rebel group, as well as being on the way, looks set to win.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for rebelling is as in 'the people are up'. 'before' is a link here, matching the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone promising and rising, making progress in a career, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Prepare to start running over second person's footprints

parts.note: over in the sense of on top of, so on
the second-person possessive is your
footprints are marks left on the ground

explanation.surface: Get ready to jog over someone else's tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare to start running' is the starter's first command in a sprint race, so it defines the call itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A race starter calls this to get sprinters into position before 'get set'.

clue.text: I name worker who is not effective

parts.note: an operative is a worker, especially in a factory

explanation.surface: I identify an employee who is not up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not working or not in force is useless, lacking effect.

clue.text: Two different articles placed on effigy in the country

indicators.note: placed on means the articles are added on after the effigy

parts.note: a guy is the effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on Bonfire Night in Britain each 5 November
the two forms of the indefinite article are an and a
the two forms of the indefinite article are an and a

explanation.surface: Somebody fixes a couple of items to a dummy in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: A GUY is the stuffed figure British children make and burn on Bonfire Night. 'in the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American state, a former British colony, has Georgetown as its capital.

clue.text: Spidery works

parts.note: read as thin, scrawly products, it really means things made by spiders

explanation.definitionFit: The silken net a spider spins is the arachnid's handiwork, its creation.

clue.text: Coloured with native pigment that's revolutionary round church first

indicators.note: first means the round letter and church come before the revolutionary

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a revolutionary, especially a communist, is a red

explanation.surface: Something painted in earth tones turns out to be a radical circling a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal but gives a ring-shaped letter; 'first' says that letter and the church come ahead of the radical. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment dug from the ground, so stained with it means tinted using that clay.

clue.text: Meddlesome person occupied with main part

parts.note: occupied means busy
the body of something is its main part, as in the body of a text

explanation.surface: A nosy parker is engaged with the central section.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prying into others' affairs is an interfering nosy parker.

clue.text: Nomads to discover extinct animal

indicators.note: to discover the hidden word, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wandering tribespeople come across the remains of a long-dead creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discover' rearranges NOMADS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric elephant-like mammal related to the mammoth, it died out thousands of years ago.

clue.text: Alas, a considerable distance off

definitions.meaning: an archaic exclamation of grief or woe
far off, as in being some way ahead or far removed

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is an old cry of sorrow; as two words, it means far from something.

clue.text: Set to get better reception when you do this

definitions.text: Set to get better reception when you do this

parts.words: Set to get better reception when you do this
parts.note: the set is a radio or TV, and adjusting it to a station improves reception

explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting a radio to a station or a broadcast is what listeners do for clear sound.

clue.text: He, an archdeacon, found endless happiness here

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, written as a
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A churchman discovered eternal bliss in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN is the abbreviation of 'the Venerable', the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England. 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the place of eternal bliss in religious belief.

clue.text: Red river

parts.note: not the American waterway but a red-coloured current flowing through the body

explanation.definitionFit: Blood is red, and the circulation is a flowing course through veins and arteries.

clue.text: One has no inclination to be dishonest on it

definitions.text: One has no inclination to be dishonest on it

parts.words: One has no inclination to be dishonest on it
parts.note: a flat surface has no slope, and someone 'on the' flat surface is honest, so feels no urge to cheat

explanation.definitionFit: A flat surface has no tilt or slope, and the idiom 'on the' plus this word means straight and honest.

clue.text: Man reportedly did not start gold lace

indicators.note: did not start means the opening letter is dropped
reportedly means as said aloud, so the name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Maurice is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man, so it is said, didn't begin trimming in gold thread.
explanation.walkthrough: MAURICE said aloud is MORRIS; 'did not start' removes the M.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lace or braid of gold or silver thread once used to trim clothing.

clue.text: Playful trick frantically contained

indicators.note: contained means the answer is held within the letters of frantically

explanation.surface: A bit of horseplay was frenziedly held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contained' points inside frANTICally.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque or silly caper, a piece of clowning, is the noun meant here.

clue.text: Beat Adam's son soundly

indicators.note: soundly means as heard, so the name of Adam's son is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: Cain was the elder son of Adam and Eve in Genesis

explanation.surface: Thrash Adam's boy thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' with 'Beat', but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone with a stick, as was once done in schools, is to beat them.

clue.text: Somersaulting repeatedly

definitions.meaning: tumbling, turning head over heels again and again

explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling head over heels turns the body round again and again, and the phrase also means many times.

clue.text: Lecturer left one man for another

indicators.note: left means departed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: Kelvin is a man's name, as in the physicist Lord Kelvin

explanation.surface: A lecturer walked out on her partner for somebody new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes L from KELVIN; 'another' then defines a different man's name. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The result is a different male first name from the one first named, a second man.

clue.text: Additional cross

definitions.meaning: the addition sign is a small upright cross

explanation.definitionFit: It means extra, an added benefit; and the addition symbol is shaped like an upright cross.

clue.text: Pineapple or other fruit not started

indicators.note: not started means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: bananas is another fruit

explanation.surface: Choose a pineapple or some other fruit that hasn't been begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not started' drops the B from BANANAS. The answer is the botanical and French name for the pineapple.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus and French name for that tropical fruit with the spiky crown.
